summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, and SVC syndrome was admitted with worsening facial and neck swelling, headaches, nausea, and blurred vision due to recurrent superior vena cava obstruction. An open SVC reconstruction with bovine pericardial patch and endarterectomy was performed successfully. Postoperatively, she developed a hematoma at the left groin line site requiring removal, and experienced a drop in hemoglobin requiring transfusion and subsequent Epogen administration. Her pain and anxiety were managed with morphine elixir, benzodiazepines, and antihistamines. She improved steadily, was ambulating independently, and was discharged home in good condition with sternal precautions, anticoagulation, and follow-up planned with her PCP in four days.
